title: Elastic-slot compactor for tail-aware prefill scheduling
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Implement an "elastic-slot" compaction layer in the runtime request packer to reduce padding overhead on mixed-length workloads by dynamically reclaiming underutilized microbatch slots and prioritizing tail requests during prefill scheduling. The feature combines (1) sequence-length profiling for adaptive bucketing, (2) a tail-dampening reclamation policy to avoid long-tail latency amplification, and (3) kernel-hint metadata emitted into the kernel scheduler so the runtime can pick attention/kv-cache kernels tuned for the actual per-slot sequence distribution.

Goals:
- Reduce aggregate padding tokens (and therefore GPU per-token cost) across production mixed workloads by 10-18%.
- Keep 95th-percentile decode latency regression under 3ms on p3/p4 class hardware under typical 95% load.
- Make kernel selection decisions cheaper by surfacing compacted slot histograms to the kernel selection engine.

Design overview:
1) Profiling pass: each request gets a lightweight seq_profile (seq_len, prefix_flag, kv_cache_size_est) emitted at enqueue time. Runtime maintains a small recent-histogram window per-worker.
2) Elastic-slot compactor: microbatches are initially formed using a loose max_seq binning. Before GPU submission, the compactor attempts to fold low-utilization slots into adjacent batches by: (a) merging short prefixes into a shared prefill segment when prefix-compatible, (b) sliding slot boundaries to consolidate trimmed tails, and (c) compacting entirely-empty padding slots into a reusable slot pool for the next submission.
3) Tail-aware prefill scheduling: requests flagged as latency-sensitive (explicit header or latency SLA profile) are given prefill priority; tail-suppressed slots are only reclaimed from non-latency-sensitive requests. We introduce a configurable tail_damping_factor to bound how aggressively we reclaim tail tokens so spikes don't penalize 95p latency.
4) Kernel hinting: when compaction completes, runtime emits an aggregated microbatch descriptor (max_seq, median_seq, pad_fraction, attention_sparsity_hint) to kernel selection. Kernel selector uses these to prefer kernels optimized for short tokens / fused KV-cache prefill paths vs. wide-seq kernels.

Algorithmic tradeoffs considered:
- Aggressive compaction reduces cost but can increase jitter for long-running decodes (risk to 95p). Mitigation: tail_damping_factor + reservation window that prevents reclaiming the last N tokens of requests flagged as high-priority.
- Compacting across prefixes can save a lot when many short prefixes exist but requires checking prefix-compatibility (cost to compare partial token hashes). We use a 64-bit prefix-signature to make this O(1) and accept false positives at a low rate.
- Kernel hinting adds metadata and a small decision path cost; our simulations show the kernel-choice benefit (~6% throughput improvement for typical short-heavy batches) offsets selection overhead.

Simulated perf (synthetic mix resembling 60/30/10 short/medium/long):
- Baseline pad fraction: 0.28; after elastic-slot compaction: 0.23 (18% reduction in padded tokens)
- Effective GPU token cost reduction: 9%
- 95p latency change: +1.6ms (within target)
Notes: simulation includes realistic KV-cache warmup and decode prefill overlap. We will validate on prod traces.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (this ticket): implement compactor + seq_profile, histogram window, and kernel-hint API. Unit tests + offline simulator hook.
- Phase 2 (follow-up): enable tail_damping, prefix-signature compatibility, and run offline replay against 7-day prod traces. Add metrics.
- Phase 3 (rollout): feature-flagged 10% traffic A/B, observe cost-per-token, 95p latency, kv-cache hit rate, memory fragmentation. Ramp to 50% then full.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit and integration tests covering compaction correctness (no token duplication, no loss).
- Offline replay shows >=8% reduction in padded tokens at 10% sample of prod traces OR no >5% regression on 95p latency.
- Kernel selector successfully receives microbatch descriptors and selects alternate kernels in at least one bench scenario (proof via logs).
- New telemetry: pad_fraction, reclaimed_slots_per_min, tail_damping_events, kernel_hint_accept_rate.

Risks and mitigations:
- Memory fragmentation due to slot pooling -> limit pool size and GC at submission boundary.
- Cross-request prefix merging correctness -> rely on prefix-signature; add strict-mode that disables merging for sensitive paths.

Rollout checklist:
- Feature flag toggles per-cluster and per-customer.
- Dashboard tile in Console (runtime) for pad_fraction and token-cost delta.
- Backstop: automatic disable if 95p latency increases by >5% for >5m.

References and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RUNTIME/pages/ELASTIC-SLOT-COMPACTOR (draft)
- Offline simulator repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-bench/tree/elastic-slot (branch)
- Early prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821
